name: Dove Lake
bio: The glacial lake beneath Cradle Mountain, reached from the Dove Lake car park, with a shoreline circuit.
reason: Inside the park's span, reached from the Cradle Mountain end; its Dove Lake Loop Track was rejected as part of this spot.

name: Cradle Mountain
bio: The 1,545 m dolerite peak that is the park's icon, seen from Dove Lake and climbed as a long day walk.
reason: Headline peak of the park; kept as a spot beside the Summit Walk (see note).

name: Overland Track
bio: Australia's most famous bushwalk: a 65 km multi-day track from Cradle Mountain south to Lake St Clair.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py found no feature; take the managing agency's point (route midpoint for a track, entrance or car park otherwise)
reason: Linear route inside the park; pinned at its midpoint (to be taken from the agency route map). Also listed by tas-west-coast-southwest, which should reference this id.

name: Lake St Clair
bio: Australia's deepest freshwater lake, at the southern end of the Overland Track, with a visitor centre and boat trips.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: photon water=lagoon (Lake St Clair Lagoon)
reason: Cynthia Bay end of the park, about 39 km from the park centre, inside the span. Wiki fixed to the Tasmanian article (the candidate's views and coordinates belonged to Michigan). Also listed by tas-west-coast-southwest; this id is the owner.

name: Marion's Lookout
bio: A steep two-hour return climb past Crater Falls and Crater Lake to a lookout over Dove Lake, with chain-assisted sections.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py found no feature; take the managing agency's point (route midpoint for a track, entrance or car park otherwise)
reason: Reached from the Dove Lake car park; inside the park span.

name: Cradle Mountain Summit Walk

coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: photon highway=path (Cradle Mount Summit Track)
reason: The route to the peak; kept as the walk beside the peak spot.

name: Mount Ossa
bio: Tasmania's highest peak at 1,617 m, climbed on a worn side track from Pelion Gap on the Overland Track.
reason: Inside the park span, reached by Overland Track walkers. Also listed by tas-west-coast-southwest; this id is the owner.

name: Pencil Pine Falls
bio: A short rainforest boardwalk past a waterfall, starting behind the Cradle Mountain Visitor Centre.
reason: Park entrance area, reached from the Cradle Mountain base.

name: Waldheim Chalet

coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: commons photo median (2 geotagged files)

name: Deloraine

coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: commons photo median (24 geotagged files)
reason: About 32 km from the park centre; the usual base for the caves (Wikivoyage lists it as gateway). Keeps its own draws beyond the Big Coffee Pot.

name: Big Coffee Pot

coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py found no feature; take the managing agency's point (route midpoint for a track, entrance or car park otherwise)
reason: Roadside icon beside Deloraine, a few minutes' photo stop.

name: Echo Point

coordinates_source: photon 'Echo Point Hut' / 'Echo Point Track' on the Lake St Clair shore; single source, LOW: check it is the Great Short Walk lookout, not only the hut
reason: Great Short Walk on the lake; see Lake St Clair re-homing note.

name: Walls of Jerusalem National Park
bio: A high-country park of dolerite peaks and tarns, known for its 43 km loop walk.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: commons photo median (31 geotagged files)
reason: A national park, never a spot of another; its only other spot is its own walk, so it stays standalone. About 28 km from Cradle Mountain's centre (inside that span) and 28 km from Mole Creek: not a spot of either because it is its own park reached from the Mersey Forest Road.

name: Walls of Jerusalem Multi-Day Walk
bio: A three to four day, 43 km loop through the park's lakes and peaks, with the Mount Jerusalem ascent.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: commons photo median (31 geotagged files)
reason: Linear route; pinned at its centre. Standalone beside the park spot: not a spot of Cradle Mountain, a different park.

name: Narawntapu National Park
bio: A coastal park with long beaches, bird hides and dusk wildlife between Devonport and Greens Beach.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py: commons photo median (3 geotagged files)
reason: Only two kept spots (with Bakers Beach), so it is a standalone spot. About 26 km from Devonport but on the Tamar side, reached from Frankford and Launceston; not a Devonport spot.
